newsitem.title: HAITI: Haiti prime minister refuses to step down.
newsitem.headline: Haiti prime minister refuses to step down.

text.p: Prime Minister Rosny Smarth and his cabinet will not be pressured by members of parliament and others who have called for their resignations, Smarth said on Thursday.
Smarth and his team have been criticised as being ineffectual to solve the impoverished country's desperate troubles, such as unemployment estimated as higher than 70 percent.

An economic plan to privatise nine state-run industries such as the electric and telephone companies has raised the ire of some groups, who have taken to the streets and virtually shut down the country one day in January.

"We don't agree that it is change in government officials that is needed," said Smarth at a party celebrating his first year in office. "It would only bring instability, which would not be good for the country."
Smarth met on Thursday with President Rene Preval, who nominated and still supports him, and members of parliament, who approved the nomination but since turned against the prime minister.

Smarth said the possibility of changing some of the ministers in his cabinet was discussed in the meeting, the second of its kind this week. But he added that the possibilities would need to be studied further before any decisions would be made.
"If we make any changes, we want to make sure it is for the better," he said.
Smarth, an agronomist nominated by Preval as part of his platform to boost agricultural production, said he would step down only if asked to by Preval.
Opposition party leader Serge Gilles said the government's critics would continue to call for new leaders, and called for a national conference between the government and the opposition.
"The situation has become so complicated, and has led to major crises," he said.

In addition to the general strike which brought the country to a standstill for a day in January, one demonstration ended in a violent clash with police in which one demonstrator's hand was blown off.

Critics of the government also pointed to both Preval and Smarth's silence on recent gang violence in a major slum outside the capital, which left at least 10 people dead and hundreds of houses burned.
